item.title: Thanksgiving Dinner Is Moving to Restaurants
item.description: [Bloomberg] Bloomberg Pursuits Food Editor Kate Krader tells Bloomberg This Weekend that more Americans are choosing restaurants for Thanksgiving as higher grocery costs, cooking stress and cleanup make dining out increasingly attractive. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Krader explains how restaurants are responding with traditional feasts and unconventional menus as Thanksgiving reservations continue to rise. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The 1982 War Still Haunts the Middle East
item.description: [Bloomberg] Journalist and author Kim Ghattas tells Bloomberg This Weekend how the violence that engulfed Lebanon in 1982 helped set the US, Israel, Iran and the wider Middle East on a trajectory that continues to shape conflicts in the region today. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini about her new book, The Best Kind of American, Ghattas examines Hezbollah’s enduring influence, Lebanon’s struggle to assert state authority and the risks of trying to remake the region through war. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Is AI a Bubble? History Offers Some Clues
item.description: [Bloomberg] Bloomberg Opinion columnist Justin Fox tells Bloomberg This Weekend that history offers warning signs for financial bubbles, but little reliable guidance about exactly when they will burst, making debt and investor sentiment important risks to watch amid the AI boom. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Fox explains why AI can be a transformative technology while its companies and investments are still vulnerable to inflated expectations and a painful market correction. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Shenzhen Wants to Become a Cultural Capital
item.description: [Bloomberg] Bloomberg’s Tiffany Ap tells Bloomberg This Weekend how Shenzhen is spending billions on museums as the technology and manufacturing hub tries to establish itself as a cultural destination and attract talent and tourism. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Ap discusses whether a city known for Huawei, Tencent and BYD can build a lasting cultural identity while rapid wealth creation and a softer broader economy deepen economic divides. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump’s Putin Outreach Tests Ukraine Talks
item.description: [Bloomberg] Bloomberg White House and National Security Editor Michelle Jamrisko tells Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump’s summit with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping reinforced his approach to diplomacy but left major questions unresolved over Ukraine and potential US security guarantees. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Jamrisko discusses European skepticism toward Putin, tensions within the Trump administration and Vice President JD Vance’s effort to distinguish his views as he looks toward 2028. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic IPO Fails to Calm AI Jitters
item.description: [Bloomberg] Seaport Research Partners Chief Equity Strategist Jonathan Golub tells Bloomberg This Weekend the sharp AI-driven market selloff looks overdone, arguing that demand for computing power remains strong and semiconductor earnings expectations continue to rise. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Golub says a bigger challenge is whether markets can keep financing the enormous capital needs of AI companies as investors are asked to fund hundreds of billions of dollars in new infrastructure. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Just Ice Tea Builds on Honest Tea’s Legacy
item.description: [Bloomberg] Just Ice Tea co-founders Seth Goldman and Spike Mendelsohn tell Bloomberg This Weekend how they built the organic tea brand after Coca-Cola discontinued Honest Tea and are expanding with Awaken, a cold-brew tea with 120 milligrams of caffeine. Speaking with host Lisa Mateo, they discuss changing consumer tastes, their approach to organic and fair-trade sourcing and why they see room for a mission-driven brand in the growing ready-to-drink tea market. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Putin Gains From Trump, Xi Summit Spotlight
item.description: [Bloomberg] Bloomberg News White House Correspondent Jeff Mason tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Vladimir Putin emerged as a key beneficiary of his historic meeting with President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, returning to the global stage alongside the US and Chinese leaders despite Russia’s continuing war in Ukraine. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Mason says the summit reflected Trump’s preference for leader-level diplomacy and explains why a Democratic-controlled Congress and Stephen Miller’s appointment as White House chief of staff are unlikely to fundamentally change the president’s foreign policy approach. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump’s Putin Ties Draw Focus After Summit
item.description: [Bloomberg] Bloomberg Economics Analyst Alex Kokcharov tells Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump’s historic meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping produced limited concrete results despite a joint declaration on energy, nuclear risks and other global issues. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Kokcharov explains what Trump’s relationship with Putin means for Ukraine as Europe takes on more of Kyiv’s support and the war intensifies after Ukraine’s latest attack on the Crimean Bridge. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'Raise Taxes, Cut Spending': Bill Dudley on the Debt
item.description: [Bloomberg] As US debt costs continue to soar, former New York Fed President Bill Dudley and Kathryn Judge of Columbia Law School discuss how to address America’s fiscal crisis, and whether Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s efforts to bring yields under control will pay off. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.description: [Bloomberg] It’s been a tough month for the stock market, rocked by back-to-back punches from the stunning ouster of Jensen Huang from Nvidia Corp. and the Democrats’ decisive victory in the midterm elections.

item.title: Anthropic Makes Its Public Market Debut

Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Ludlow also examines the turmoil at Nvidia following Jensen Huang’s departure and the uncertainty surrounding the chipmaker’s search for new leadership.
